overview.problem: Current documentation (docs/guide.html) is disorganized, lacks a storyline, and serves neither new users nor experienced users well. It's a reference document disguised as a guide, with no progressive disclosure or clear reading path.
overview.goal: Reorganize documentation following Diátaxis framework principles. Four distinct documentation types serve four distinct user needs: learning (tutorials), doing (how-to guides), information (reference), understanding (explanation).
overview.approach: Split into multiple HTML pages organized by Diátaxis quadrant. Each document type has its own conventions, audience, and purpose. Navigation reflects the four types explicitly.

diataxisPrinciples.tutorial: Learning-oriented experiences. User DOES something under guidance. Serves STUDY (skill acquisition). Minimal explanation, concrete steps, reliable success.
diataxisPrinciples.howto: Goal-oriented directions. Addresses real-world problems. Serves WORK (skill application). Assumes competent user. Practical, action-focused.
diataxisPrinciples.reference: Information-oriented technical description. Facts, neutral, complete. Serves WORK. Structured like the machinery it describes.
diataxisPrinciples.explanation: Understanding-oriented discussion. Context, background, why. Serves STUDY. Discursive, can contain opinions and perspectives.

audiences.name: studying
audiences.description: User is learning, building skills and understanding

audiences.name: working
audiences.description: User is competent and trying to accomplish something specific
audiences.needs: How-to guides (practical directions) and Reference (facts to consult)

phases.name: Foundation
phases.description: Create one tutorial (quickstart) and one explanation (concepts). These serve users in STUDY mode - learning and understanding.

sections.title: Quickstart
sections.diataxisPurpose: Learning-oriented experience. User DOES something under guidance to acquire skills.
sections.goal: Get a new user from 'never heard of Struktur' to 'I extracted my first JSON' in under 5 minutes with reliable success.

diataxisPrinciples.teacherStudentRelationship: You are the absent instructor. User follows your directions. You are responsible for their success.
diataxisPrinciples.minimalExplanation: Don't try to teach by explaining. Allow learning through doing. Link to explanation for later.
diataxisPrinciples.concreteSteps: Focus on THIS problem, THIS action, THIS result. Concrete leads to general understanding.
diataxisPrinciples.reliableSuccess: Every step must produce the expected result. Confidence builds layer by layer.
diataxisPrinciples.firstPersonPlural: Use 'we' to affirm the tutor-learner relationship: 'In this tutorial, we will...'

sections.title: What we'll build
sections.content: One-sentence promise: 'Extract structured data from any file in 3 commands'. Show the learner where they'll be going.
sections.diataxisNote: Not 'you will learn' - that's presumptuous. Describe what WE will accomplish together.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.content: List: Node.js 18+ or Bun installed, An API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google)

sections.title: Step 1: Install

sections.diataxisNote: Each step should produce visible results. Show expected output.

sections.title: Step 2: Configure your provider
sections.content: Two methods: (1) Quick: environment variable export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-..., (2) Secure: struktur auth set --provider openai (reads from stdin)

sections.title: Step 3: Extract your first data

commands: echo 'Invoice #1234 from Acme Corp. Total: $1,250.00. Due: March 15, 2026.' > invoice.txt

sections.diataxisNote: Point out what the learner should notice. Close the loops of learning.

sections.title: What happened?
sections.content: BRIEF explanation: 'We used the simple strategy to extract data.' Minimal. Link to concepts for understanding.
sections.diataxisNote: This is NOT the place for extended explanation. Just enough to orient the learner. Link to explanation docs.

sections.title: Where to go from here
sections.content: Links organized by Diátaxis type: Tutorials (none - you're done!), How-to (Choose a strategy), Reference (CLI, API), Explanation (Concepts)
sections.diataxisNote: Help the learner transition from STUDY to WORK. They can now use how-to guides and reference.

sections.title: Concepts
sections.diataxisPurpose: Understanding-oriented discussion. Serves users in STUDY mode who need to understand WHY and build mental models.
sections.goal: Help users understand how Struktur works so they can make informed decisions. This is NOT a guide to action - it's for understanding.

diataxisPrinciples.discursive: Can circle around the subject, approach from different directions
diataxisPrinciples.whyQuestions: Answers 'why' - why this design, why these concepts
diataxisPrinciples.linksToOthers: Links to reference for facts, how-to for action

sections.title: What is Struktur?
sections.content: One-paragraph definition. Frame as 'a data extraction harness'. Mention what it does NOT do (parse files, stream) to set expectations.
keyPoints: TypeScript extraction engine using Vercel AI SDK
Turns pre-parsed artifacts into validated JSON
Handles chunking, strategies, validation, merging
Does NOT parse PDFs/HTML - you handle that upstream

sections.title: The Extraction Pipeline
sections.content: Visual diagram showing the flow: Input -> Artifacts -> Strategy -> Output. Validation happens INSIDE strategies (strategy-dependent) AND after the strategy completes.

diagram.strategyInternals: Strategy contains: Chunking, LLM calls with validation+retry, Merge/Dedupe (if applicable)

sections.designNotes: This diagram is the central visual anchor for the entire mental model

sections.title: Artifacts: The input format
sections.content: What is an artifact? Why normalized input? Structure overview. How to create them.
keyPoints: Artifacts are JSON DTOs with text and media slices
Struktur doesn't parse files - you provide normalized artifacts
Structure: id, type, contents[], media[]
Creation: --input, --stdin, fileToArtifact(), urlToArtifact()

sections.title: Strategies: The orchestration
sections.content: What is a strategy? A strategy orchestrates the entire extraction: chunking, LLM calls, validation, and merging. Each strategy handles these differently.
keyPoints: A strategy defines HOW extraction happens
simple: single-shot for small inputs
parallel, sequential, auto-merge, double-pass for larger/complex inputs
Validation happens INSIDE the strategy with automatic retries
Merge/dedupe behavior is strategy-dependent
links: strategy-selection.html for choosing the right strategy

sections.title: Validation
sections.content: JSON Schema + Ajv validation. IMPORTANT: Validation is integrated into strategies, not a separate phase. Strategies validate each LLM output and retry on failure. There's also a final validation after the strategy completes.
keyPoints: Validation is strategy-internal: each LLM call is validated
On validation failure, errors are fed back to LLM for retry
Most extractions converge within 2 attempts
Final validation happens after strategy completes

sections.title: Merge & Dedupe
sections.content: Merge and dedupe behavior is strategy-dependent. Only multi-chunk strategies (parallel, sequential, doublePass) need merging. Auto-merge variants include deduplication.
keyPoints: Merge behavior varies by strategy
parallel/sequential use LLM merge
auto-merge variants use schema-aware merge + dedupe
Dedupe has two stages: hash-based + LLM-based

sections.title: How to choose a strategy
sections.diataxisPurpose: Goal-oriented guide. Addresses a real-world problem: 'Which strategy should I use?' Assumes competent user.
sections.goal: Help users who know they need to extract data choose the right strategy for their situation.

diataxisPrinciples.actionOriented: Title says HOW to do something
diataxisPrinciples.assumesCompetence: User knows what they want (extraction); they need practical guidance
diataxisPrinciples.noTeaching: No explanation of what strategies are - link to Concepts for that
diataxisPrinciples.practicalOnly: Focus on decision criteria and trade-offs
diataxisPrinciples.realWorldComplexity: Acknowledge edge cases and help user adapt guidance

sections.title: Problem: Choosing the right strategy
sections.content: You need to extract data and want the best strategy for your situation. This guide helps you decide.
sections.diataxisNote: State the problem from user's perspective, not from the tool's.

sections.title: Quick decision guide
sections.content: Decision tree with clear if-then rules: If input fits in context -> simple. If speed matters -> parallel. If context across chunks matters -> sequential. If both speed and accuracy -> doublePass. If dedup needed -> auto-merge variants.
sections.diataxisNote: Practical directions for real-world situations. No theory.

sections.title: Strategy comparison
sections.content: Table comparing all strategies on: speed, accuracy, context preservation, best for, token usage
sections.diataxisNote: Reference material embedded in how-to is acceptable when it serves the practical goal.

sections.title: Use simple when...
sections.content: Documents fit in context window, simple schemas, quick testing. No special concerns.
sections.diataxisNote: Conditional imperatives: 'If you want x, do y.'

sections.title: Use parallel when...
sections.content: Speed is priority, chunks are independent, large document sets. Accept: may miss cross-chunk context.
sections.diataxisNote: State trade-offs clearly so user can make informed decision.

sections.title: Use sequential when...
sections.content: Context between chunks matters, building data incrementally. Accept: slower than parallel.

sections.title: Use auto-merge variants when...
sections.content: Extracting arrays that may have duplicates, consolidating results. Need dedup without LLM merge cost.

sections.title: Use double-pass when...
sections.content: High-stakes extractions, complex schemas, quality > cost. Willing to pay for two passes.

sections.title: Strategies overview
sections.content: Strategies orchestrate extraction: chunking, LLM calls, validation with retries, merging. Each strategy implements these differently.
sections.diataxisNote: Brief factual summary. For choosing a strategy, see how-to guide.

sections.title: Common behavior across all strategies
sections.content: All strategies: (1) Use JSON schema for structured output, (2) Validate each LLM call with Ajv, (3) Retry on validation failure, (4) Final validation after completion.

sections.title: simple
sections.content: Single-shot extraction for small inputs.
algorithm: If exceeds token budget, chunk to fit
sections.validationBehavior: One validation per LLM call, with retries on failure.
sections.diataxisNote: Pure facts about behavior. No recommendation.

sections.title: parallel
sections.content: Concurrent batch processing, then LLM merge.
sections.validationBehavior: Each chunk's LLM output validated with retries. Merge step also validated.
sections.mergeBehavior: LLM-based. Separate LLM call combines all partial outputs.
sections.characteristics: Fast but may miss cross-chunk context. LLM merge adds token cost.

sections.title: sequential
sections.content: Process chunks in order, passing previous results as context.
algorithm: Each chunk receives previous extraction results as context
sections.validationBehavior: Each chunk's LLM output validated with retries.
sections.mergeBehavior: Context-based accumulation. Each LLM call receives previous results.
sections.characteristics: Slower than parallel but maintains coherence across chunks.

sections.title: parallelAutoMerge
sections.content: Parallel extraction with schema-aware merge and deduplication.
sections.validationBehavior: Each chunk's LLM output validated with retries.
sections.mergeBehavior: Schema-aware. Arrays concatenate, objects shallow-merge, scalars prefer new values. No LLM merge step.
sections.dedupeBehavior: Two-stage: (1) CRC32 hash for exact duplicates, (2) LLM for semantic duplicates.

sections.title: sequentialAutoMerge
sections.content: Sequential extraction with schema-aware merge and deduplication.
sections.validationBehavior: Each chunk's LLM output validated with retries.
sections.mergeBehavior: Schema-aware merge after each sequential step.

sections.title: doublePass
sections.content: Parallel pass for speed, sequential pass for refinement.
algorithm: Second pass: sequential refinement with first-pass result as context
sections.validationBehavior: Each LLM call validated with retries. Both passes validated.
sections.mergeBehavior: LLM merge after first pass. Sequential pass refines the merged result.
sections.characteristics: Highest quality, highest token cost. Two full passes.

sections.title: doublePassAutoMerge
sections.content: Parallel + auto-merge + sequential refinement.
sections.validationBehavior: Each LLM call validated with retries.
sections.mergeBehavior: Schema-aware merge (no LLM merge). Sequential pass refines.
sections.dedupeBehavior: Full two-stage dedupe before refinement pass.
